frozen_original_summary.title: EEOC Gutted — Trump Fires 3 of 5 Commissioners
frozen_original_summary.claim: Three of five commissioners fired on January 20.

same_event_evidence.fact: Trump removed EEOC Commissioners Jocelyn Samuels and Charlotte Burrows late Monday, January 27, 2025, and also fired General Counsel Karla Gilbride.
same_event_evidence.quote: EEOC Commissioners Jocelyn Samuels and Charlotte Burrows said Trump removed them from their posts late on Monday. Trump also fired the agency's general counsel, Karla Gilbride.
same_event_evidence.source_excerpt: Jan 28 (Reuters) - U.S. President Donald Trump has fired at least two Democratic members of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. EEOC Commissioners Jocelyn Samuels and Charlotte Burrows said Trump removed them from their posts late on Monday. Trump also fired the agency's general counsel, Karla Gilbride.

same_event_evidence.fact: The removals left the already-vacant five-member commission without a quorum of three.
same_event_evidence.quote: leaves it without a quorum of three commissioners
same_event_evidence.source_excerpt: The five-member commission already had a vacancy, so firing Samuels and Burrows leaves it without a quorum of three commissioners.

same_event_evidence.fact: AP likewise reports two commissioners were dismissed late Monday night before their five-year terms expired.
same_event_evidence.quote: The two commissioners of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, Charlotte Burrows and Jocelyn Samuels, confirmed in statements Tuesday that they were fired late Monday night.
same_event_evidence.source_excerpt: The two commissioners of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, Charlotte Burrows and Jocelyn Samuels, confirmed in statements Tuesday that they were fired late Monday night. Both said they were exploring options to challenge their dismissals, calling their removal before the expiration of their five-year terms an unprecedented decision that undermines the agency’s independence.

terminal_record.same_event_summary: Frozen parent says January 20 and three commissioners. The retrieved Reuters/AP reports identify two EEOC commissioners, Burrows and Samuels, removed late Monday January 27, 2025, plus general counsel Karla Gilbride; Reuters says an existing vacancy meant the two removals left no quorum. Existing entry-5842 covers these same January 27 EEOC removals as part of the same-day NLRB action. Entry-6274 also overlaps but its title says all EEOC commissioners, so entry-5842 is the precise survivor.

preserve_supported_facts: Two EEOC commissioners, not three, were removed late January 27, 2025.
General Counsel Karla Gilbride was also fired.
The prior vacancy plus two removals left the five-member commission without a quorum; Reuters described which commission actions were blocked.

The EEOC was wholly unable to pursue all cases.

impact_proposal.confidence_reason: Reuters and AP directly report the removals, commissioners' terms, and quorum effect; legal permissibility and longer-term consequences were not resolved in these reports.
impact_proposal.rationale: Removing two commissioners from a federal employment-discrimination agency left it without the quorum needed for specified commission actions. This is a material institutional interruption, while the cited reports do not establish harm to individual claimants, a final legal ruling, or a lasting effect.

uncertainties: The January 2025 reports say legal challenges were being considered; they do not establish a final legal ruling.
The entry's more-than-70,000 annual charge figure and claim that the agency was wholly crippled are not needed to describe this event and are omitted.
